reviewer: Codex, independent; did not author v1, v2, or v3
protocol: Independent successor review; refute claimed repairs; other current v3 reviewer not read
reviewScope: Review only. This review does not mark DR-112 SATISFIED, does not qualify or demonstrate anything, does not authorize implementation, and does not apply or seal the candidate.
summary: v3 genuinely repairs the stale-then-expired ordering, RECOVERY clock handling, unmatched-guard fallback, monotonic repeated observations, explicit abort event, envelope-inactive fail closure, the 343-triple continuation table, candidate finding-id attribution, and historical/diff honesty. It is still not acceptable. A recovery-typed payload from UNBOOTSTRAPPED can match both the bootstrap-to-TRUSTED and ceremony-staging transitions, while ST-RECOVERY/PRESENT is duplicated; the relation therefore lacks disjoint guards and can skip the recovery ceremony. More seriously, RECOVER-COMMIT targets TRUSTED without applying the complete trustPolicyShape, and recoveryAuthorityShape names an authority set without requiring authorization evidence from that set over the old-root-to-new-root transition. The audit rule requires refusalReason, but named install and continuation refusals have no reason mapping and the accepted abort text conflicts with the no-reason-on-accepted rule. DR-112 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes no implementation.

blockers.title: Recovery-payload dispatch is not guard-disjoint and can bypass the recovery ceremony
blockers.measurement: The v3 machine has 7 states, 9 events, and 20 transition members. Expansion yields 43 distinct named state/event pairs and 20 fallback-only pairs. Six pairs have multiple transition members. Four ordinary-refresh/staging overlaps are intended to be split by payload kind and the two TRUSTED/CLOCK rows have complementary guards, but the split is not complete. For ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED/EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD, transition 0 accepts any complete payload satisfying the bootstrap trust predicate after activation and targets ST-TRUSTED; transition 7 accepts a recovery-typed payload and targets same/ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED for staging. Transition 0 never says ordinary/non-recovery, and airGapPayload defines no authenticated payload-kind discriminator. A complete, trust-valid payload labeled recovery-typed therefore satisfies both written guards and has two targets.
blockers.ceremonyBypass: The staging row promises that a recovery-typed payload does not skip EV-RECOVER-BEGIN, and FC-RECOVER requires UNBOOTSTRAPPED recovery to stage, begin, then commit. The competing bootstrap row reaches ST-TRUSTED directly without recoveryAuthorityShape or EV-RECOVER-BEGIN. If statePrecedence is used to select between the two declared rows, its written order ranks ST-TRUSTED above ST-UNBOOTSTRAPPED, choosing the ceremony-bypassing target; if it is not used, the relation is multi-target. Either reading violates the claimed deterministic recovery staging repair.
blockers.duplicateRow: ST-RECOVERY/EV-PRESENT-PAYLOAD is declared twice, at transitions 3 and 19, with overlapping 'Recovery payload only' guards and the same state target. The earlier copy retains the now-false v2 parenthetical that abort remains an EV-RECOVER-BEGIN failure/default refusal; the later copy names EV-RECOVER-ABORT. Even though the state target agrees, the contract does not say whether one or two transition/audit actions fire or which guard text is authoritative.
blockers.whyBlocker: DR-112 requires a reviewed state machine and a recovery ceremony. A caller-controlled or undefined payload classification that can choose direct TRUSTED entry instead of ceremony staging is a recovery-boundary bypass, not a cosmetic duplicate.
blockers.minimumRepair: Define an authenticated ordinary-versus-recovery payload discriminator in the payload shape, make every overlapping PRESENT guard explicitly disjoint, and state that recovery-typed input from every recovery source including UNBOOTSTRAPPED can only stage. Remove the duplicate ST-RECOVERY/PRESENT row and its stale abort text. Re-expand the guarded relation, not just the state/event pair set, and add a fixture whose recovery-typed UNBOOTSTRAPPED payload would otherwise satisfy the ordinary bootstrap predicate.

blockers.title: RECOVER-COMMIT still skips the complete TRUSTED-entry predicate and does not require positive recovery authorization
blockers.measurement: Five transition members target ST-TRUSTED. Bootstrap, refresh, and install either name trustPolicyShape or explicitly reuse the first-bootstrap predicate. RECOVER-COMMIT does not. Its guard requires only that TRUSTED-entry be ACTIVE and recoveryAuthorityShape hold. ACTIVE means that the envelope mechanism/dependency is enabled; transition 4 demonstrates that activation and satisfying trustPolicyShape are separate predicates by requiring both. Commit therefore omits the byte-level pass, envelope verification over the recovery payload, role/delegated-namespace authorization, signer-threshold evaluation, expiry/future-time check, and revocation-freshness check that requiredOnEveryTrustedEntry says are mandatory. FC-RECOVER mirrors the same weakened condition rather than closing it.
blockers.authorizationGap: recoveryAuthorityShape requires identification of the old root, existence of a reserved authority set distinct from the replacement root's self-signature, a negative rule that the new root not self-authorize, and counter advance. It never requires signatures/approval from that authority set, satisfaction of its reserved threshold, or a signed binding over the identified old root and replacement root. Naming a set and forbidding sole self-signature is not a positive authorization relation; an implementation cannot decide what non-self evidence authorizes the replacement.
blockers.whyBlocker: The accepted DR-103/DR-112 split leaves ceremony-valid envelope, key, threshold, rotation, and recovery semantics to this row. A recovery transition cannot enter a state named TRUSTED without the complete applicable trust predicate and proof that the reserved recovery authority authorized this specific root replacement.
blockers.minimumRepair: Define and reference a recoveryTrustedEntry predicate on RECOVER-COMMIT: every applicable trustPolicyShape check, with bootstrapAnchorCustody replaced by a positive authorization from recoveryAuthoritySet; byte/envelope verification; threshold satisfaction against the reserved parameter; an old-root/new-root/role binding; expiry/future/freshness checks; and anti-rollback. Keep all cardinalities and identities reserved. Extend fixtures with a payload that has a named authority set but no valid approval from it, plus expired, wrong-role, and bad-envelope recovery commits.

shouldFix.title: The required refusalReason invariant has no total mapping and conflicts with the abort record
shouldFix.detail: auditAndWaiver now correctly says refusalReason is required exactly on refused outcomes, but the machine does not define one for every refusal. The named non-TRUSTED EV-INSTALL row refuses directly and therefore never falls through to fallbackByEvent, yet supplies no reason identity. EV-CONTINUE is named for every state by a wildcard transition; its policy rows say continue/refuse but define no refusal reasons. Its fallback entry cannot repair that: it uses the non-enum outcome 'see-offlineRunningPolicy' and the placeholder reason 'as-totalDecision-or-defaultRefuse', and the fallback is not selected while the wildcard guard matches. FC-REFUSAL-AUDIT asserts fallback/guard-false refusals but omits these named policy refusals.
shouldFix.abortConflict: EV-RECOVER-ABORT says the abort event outcome is accepted while also saying it is audited with refusalReason RECOVERY-ABORTED 'on the ceremony'. The only declared event-audit schema forbids refusalReason when outcome is accepted, and no separate ceremony-termination record shape is defined. The text therefore either violates the invariant in one record or relies on an undeclared second record.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Declare a closed refusal-reason vocabulary and a total mapping for every refused named transition, guard-false fallback, and continuation decision. Accepted audit records must omit refusalReason rather than carry a value or placeholder. If ceremony termination needs its own reason, define a distinct ceremony audit record and its join to the accepted abort event. Expand FC-REFUSAL-AUDIT to named install and continuation refusals.

advisories.title: EV-RECOVER-ABORT uses an undeclared transition-target token
advisories.detail: The abort transition's to value is 'computed', which is neither one of the seven state ids nor the established 'same' meta-target. The guard prose bounds the result to REVOKED, QUORUM-LOST, EXPIRED, STALE-REVOCATION, or UNBOOTSTRAPPED under the declared precedence and explicitly forbids TRUSTED, so this is not independently safety-blocking. A structured target function or explicit guarded rows would make conformance and audit-to-state validation mechanical.
